gaps.construct: a and x are any comparable type; with key, items are T and x is K
gaps.description: The doc uses `of T` only inside a type declaration and never shows an operation introducing type parameters or bounding them by an ordering (`K supports is less than`).

gaps.construct: key=None parameter holding a function, called as key(a[mid])
gaps.description: There is no type for an operation value and no syntax for calling an operation held in a variable; `maybe operation taking a T producing a K` and `key_function (item mid of a)` are invented.

gaps.construct: when key is None, x is compared directly with items of a
gaps.description: The no-key branch needs T and K to be the same type, which depends on a runtime value; nothing in the doc can relate a type parameter to whether an optional argument is present.

gaps.construct: lo=0, hi=None, *, key=None (defaults and a keyword-only argument)
gaps.description: No defaults or keyword arguments, so every caller must pass all four, using `nothing` for absent ones and a label word in place of the keyword name.

gaps.construct: rebinding the parameters lo and hi inside the loop
gaps.description: Parameters are not shown as mutable, so they are copied into `var low` and `var high`; `choose` is a statement, so `high` needs a dummy start value before the `choose` sets it.

gaps.construct: if hi is None: hi = len(a)
gaps.description: Unwrapping a maybe with a fallback takes a full five-line `choose` because there is no expression form like `hi or else count of a`.
The doc never says whether `/` on Int truncates, floors or produces a fraction.

gaps.construct: a[mid] raising IndexError when hi exceeds len(a)
gaps.description: The doc does not say what `item i of items` does out of range (failure, precondition, or compile-time proof obligation), so the failure behaviour for a too-large hi is unspecified.

gaps.construct: docstring guarantee in terms of the defaulted hi; 'a is sorted' by key
gaps.description: The `sorted` predicate is defined only for List of Int and not for sorting by a key; the postcondition depends on the resolved hi, which exists only in the body, so the ensure is limited to the default case.

gaps.construct: raise ValueError('lo must be non-negative') with a message
gaps.description: `because` is shown only on header clauses; it is unclear whether a `fail with` statement can carry a message. Python's key() and __lt__ can also raise arbitrary exceptions, which a `fails with` list cannot state without knowing them.

invented_syntax: maybe operation taking a T producing a K
fail with ValueError because "lo must be non-negative"
notes: The two duplicated loops in the original exist for speed; with a callable key the natural Scribe form would be one loop, but merging them needs either a default identity operation or the type-level link between T and K. Python duck-typed comparisons (`<` raising TypeError on mixed types) have no counterpart, which makes the Scribe version stricter than the original. Label words for four parameters (`x in a from lo to hi by key`) already reads awkwardly and suggests label words do not scale past two or three arguments.
